decision: Verification = (1) by construction: knowledge is verbatim spans with hash-checked sources, so only span-vs-claim needs checking; (2) exact rules for numbers/negation; (3) a small domain checker distilled from synthetic hard negatives generated from OUR spans (number change, negation, qualifier drop, scope over-reach) plus funnel verdicts and corrections as real labels; (4) strong model (Claude/qwen14b) only on the uncertain slice
evidence: Measured: off-the-shelf free checkers 13-15/31 bad accepted vs paid Gemini 9/31 at 4% good rejected (not significant; A4); no grader passes planted errors (M6-T1: Claude 11/40 FP, mostly dropped qualifiers; numbers solved by exact checks); stacking correlated judges adds nothing (M5-T1, n_eff ~2). Vendor pattern (FineWeb-Edu, DCLM, MiniCheck, HHEM): a strong labeler labels a sample or generates synthetic hard cases, a small cheap classifier is trained on them and runs over everything, rules catch the obvious cases, the strong model only spot-checks. Lookup gap found: the consumption repo (PLAN, modules, results) is not in the engine.
outcome: Step 1 PASS (2,000 synthetic pairs from our own spans, blind label audit 39/40). Step 2 FAIL: cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-xsmall on CPU, 936 SCREEN rows, threshold at 36/905 good rejected: zero-shot 28/31 bad accepted; fine-tuned 1 epoch on the 2,000 pairs 27/31 (bar <= 9/31). Training loss fell to ~0.02, so the model learned the synthetic edits (scope/negation/number/qualifier), but that does not transfer to the real bad rows, which are over-reach. Conclusion: a small checker distilled from edit-generated negatives does not work for our error type; the vendor recipe needs labels of the real error distribution, which we do not have in volume. Verification layer 1 (verbatim span + hash) stands on its own; layers 3-4 are not demonstrated. G4 stays open. Code: /home/claude/d008 (cloud) train.py, gen.py.

Gate rows: true rescued 1/4 (126) (bar >= 3/4: FAIL); bad rescued 1/3 (58) (bar 0/3: FAIL). Safety: bad rescued 12/18 across all even bad rows. Secondary +calc rows: true 4/4, bad 2/2. Cause: (a) 3 of 4 true 'number' rejections cite numbers ABSENT from the passage (66: 75.3; 158: 26, 40.0; 202: ~100%): missing context, a source-open problem, not formatting; (b) bad claims usually carry correct numbers (the error is over-reach / association), so number-set match is necessary, never sufficient; (c) the one-step arithmetic search finds coincidences (600/50*100=1200; 0-1=-1). Not usable as a rescue. At most a feature for the judge (numbers-consistent flag), with no arithmetic search.
